activity_context.topic_title: Newton's Method for Optimizing Multivariable Functions

feedback.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,2]\times [0,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)={x}^{2}{y}^{2}-3{x}^{2}y-{x}^{2}-2xy+4x.
$$

Calculate one iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at ${x}_{0}=[1,\,1]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to **three decimal places.**

| ${x}_{1}≈[$ | {{field-1}} | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-2}} |  |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}-3{x}^{2}y-{x}^{2}-2xy+4x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}-3{x}^{2}y-{x}^{2}-2xy+4x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x{y}^{2}-6xy-2x-2y+4 \\ 2{x}^{2}y-3{x}^{2}-2x\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x{y}^{2}-6xy-2x-2y+4) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{2}y-3{x}^{2}-2x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(2x{y}^{2}-6xy-2x-2y+4) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(2{x}^{2}y-3{x}^{2}-2x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2}-6y-2 & 4xy-6x-2 \\ 4xy-6x-2 & 2{x}^{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2}-6y-2 & 4xy-6x-2 \\ 4xy-6x-2 & 2{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}2x{y}^{2}-6xy-2x-2y+4 \\ 2{x}^{2}y-3{x}^{2}-2x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with
${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-{[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2}-6y-2 & 4xy-6x-2 \\ 4xy-6x-2 & 2{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}2x{y}^{2}-6xy-2x-2y+4 \\ 2{x}^{2}y-3{x}^{2}-2x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}2(1)^{2}-6(1)-2 & 4(1)(1)-6(1)-2 \\ 4(1)(1)-6(1)-2 & 2(1)^{2}\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2(1)(1)^{2}-6(1)(1)-2(1)-2(1)+4 \\ 2(1)^{2}(1)-3(1)^{2}-2(1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-6 & -4 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{(-6)\cdot 2-(-4)\cdot (-4)}[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 4 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{28}[\begin{aligned}-20 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}0.286 \\ 1.071\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
